hook.text: Gold nanorods absorb near-infrared light and convert it to heat — a focused laser cooks the tumor.

buildup.text: Near-infrared light penetrates several centimeters into tissue — reaching tumors that visible light cannot.

discovery.text: Gold nanorods tuned to absorb at 800 nm heat up intensely — a few milliwatts raise local temperature by 20°C.

twist.text: Once the nanorods overheat and reshape into spheres, they lose their NIR absorption — treatment stops working.

climax.text: AuroLase therapy for prostate cancer uses gold nanoshells and NIR laser — clinical trials show tumor ablation.

punchline.text: Shine a laser on gold nanorods and they become tiny heaters.

quiz.question: Why are gold nanorods used for photothermal therapy?
options: They emit radiation that kills cancer cells
They efficiently absorb near-infrared light and convert it to localized heat
They deliver chemotherapy drugs inside the tumor
